llm_text: I disagree — U.S. engagement in the global economy isn’t inherently bad because it brings lower prices, bigger markets, and innovation, but those gains shouldn’t come at the expense of American workers and communities. llm_text: US involvement in the global economy can cost jobs and put downward pressure on wages in the short run, but access to bigger markets, innovation, and lower prices tends to benefit the US long-term. We should support displaced workers—not retreat from trade.

llm_text: I disagree — U.S. engagement in the global economy isn’t broadly bad; it brings jobs, lower prices, access to critical resources, and innovation that strengthen the country over time.
